newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil futures end firmer but off the highs.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil futures end firmer but off the highs.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures ended firmer but off the highs on Wednesday. Traders said the gains were supported by stronger crude and NYMEX products futures.
April gas oil futures last traded $2.00 firmer at $167.25 a tonne after touch an intra-day high of $168.50.
Analysts said that gas oil, while technically weak, was still oversold on the weekly charts and because of this the market would find it hard to move lower in the next few days.
In excess of 500,000 tonnes of gas oil from NW Europe and the Mediterranean has moved to the Far East and South America recently and this has steadied physical gas oil.
It has also lifted poor European refining margins a little, traders said.

"The margins are awful. They have come up a bit from the end of last week with support from gas oil but many complex refineries are running at break even. Simple refineries are making a loss," one UK refiner said.

API inventory data showed U.S. distillate stocks up 197,000 barrels but traders said the market preferred to focus on slightly bullish gasoline data showing a drop in U.S. gasoline output as the industry gears up for the spring and summer driving seasons.
Production fell 137,000 barrels per day in the latest week to 7.24 million bpd.
Physical delivery against the expired IPE March gas oil futures contract which settled $1 firmer at $164.25 a tonne will be 1,482 lots, or 148,200 tonnes, an IPE official said on Wednesday.
Deliveries against the February contract were 585,500 tonnes and 261,000 tonnes against January.
The April Brent crude contract stood 26 cents up at $19.50 a barrel with the April/May backwardation around +20 cents up from +10 cents in early business.
Aggressive buying by a Wall Street trader also widened the North Sea Brent April/May spread sharply to trade several times at a high of +22 cents, having fetched just +6 cents in earlier business.
"(The trading house) just moved in and bought everything it could in half an hour. Looks like it's expecting a strong April market," said one dealer.
